title: Account start
summary: Opens the account that lives on this phone. Device-first accounts have no login screen (ADR 0057): the app signs in with the hidden password from the device credential store, then restores the session on later starts.

phase.description: opening: restoring a session, finishing a pending sign-up or signing in. noAccount: no session and no device credential; the app shows onboarding-welcome. failed: the sign-in or restore failed. ready: the session runs and the app shows chat-list.

userId.description: The Matrix ID of the account, when one is known.

legacyKept.description: true when phase is noAccount and this phone holds data of the earlier Bipe app (the fork, same app ID) that this app could not open yet: on iOS a keychain item in a legacy read group whose service this app never writes, on Android the fork's vault kept as bipe-account.fork or a SharedPreferences file this app never writes. Nothing of it is deleted or overwritten (bipe-chat/bipe#603).

start.effect: On launch: restore the saved SDK session if one exists; else finish a pending sign-up with POST /v1/signup/resume (signup-create, ADR 0094); else read the device credentials of every account on this phone (BipeKit BipeCredentialStore.password() on iOS, libraries/bipe on Android) and sign in with it; else go to noAccount. Before noAccount it checks for legacy data (legacyKept).

recoverLegacy.effect: From legacyKept: opens recovery-start ("Já tenho conta"), where the synced recovery token of the earlier app (iCloud Keychain, Block Store) or the e-mail path gets the account back.

startFresh.effect: From legacyKept: shows onboarding-welcome for this launch. The legacy data stays on the phone; the next launch checks again.

notes: Sign-in uses MAS compatibility login (m.login.password on /_matrix/client/v3/login). bipe-infra compose/templates/mas-bipe.yaml keeps passwords.enabled true for this.
The homeserver comes from the build configuration, never from the user.
The SDK session store and the saved session live in the app group (iOS) or app storage (Android), so the switch from the fork can reuse them (client-rewrite-study.md section 6).

Sign-up is onboarding-welcome to signup-done (bipe-chat/bipe#553). Recovery, the PIN entry and the app lock are bipe-chat/bipe#555. Until a build has sign-up, noAccount shows bipe_app_start_no_account_title and bipe_app_start_no_account_body.

While a recovery started on this phone is kept (recovery-waiting), start opens that screen instead of noAccount. A recovery that waits for this account on another phone shows recovery-alert after ready.
Never log or show the password or the recovery token.

Several accounts (ADR 0086): account-start opens every account on the phone. The current account is the one used last on this phone (saved by app-tabs switchAccount). On the first start, with nothing saved, it is the oldest account on the phone (the credential stored first), so the primary account opens, not a newer second one.

Carry-over from the fork (bipe/docs/client-switch-plan.md step 3, bipe-chat/bipe#603): with the store ID set the app reads the earlier app's data in place and copies what it can read (keychain move on iOS, BipeForkVault on Android). It never deletes, moves over or writes into a legacy item, except the one move of the fork's vault file to bipe-account.fork on Android, which keeps every byte.

Never show an empty chat list or onboarding-welcome as if the phone had no account while legacyKept is true: noAccount shows bipe_app_start_legacy_title, bipe_app_start_legacy_body, then bipe_app_start_legacy_recover (recoverLegacy, primary) and bipe_app_start_legacy_fresh (startFresh).
Account isolation: every legacy item maps to the one Matrix ID it names. An item without a Matrix ID is never given to an account; it shows up only in the structure report.

Structure report (rehearsal evidence, bipe-chat/bipe#603): when legacy data is on the phone, problem-report adds it as one more compressed-log file, legacy-data.json, only when includeLogs is on. It lists names, sizes, value types, JSON key names and SQLite table names; never a value, a password, a token, a key, a message or a Matrix ID (Matrix IDs show as their server name only).
